newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. comptroller decides not to challenge Pataki.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. comptroller decides not to challenge Pataki.

text.p: New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall, seen as a top Democrat challenger to Gov. George Pataki, said Thursday he would seek re-election next year and not run against the Republican governor.
Explaining it had not been an easy decision, McCall said he felt he could best serve New York State by monitoring its finances.

"I believe the answer to the question--how I can best serve--is by continuing to be the people's fiscal watchdog, working to implement the reforms and changes necessary to bring New York into the 21st century. That's why I've decided to seek another term as state comptroller in 1998."
McCall, an African American, has said he had qualms about the fund-raising needed to mount a gubernatorial challenge.
The comptroller's decision leaves the field open to several potential candidates, including New York City Council Speaker Peter Vallone, a Democrat who has not announced whether he will run.

There has been speculation that a few of the individuals, like Charles Schumer, a Democrat Congressman from Brooklyn, who plan to challenge U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato, a Republican, instead might opt to run against Pataki.
